matchstick.title: Check arithmetic validity
matchstick.principle: After moving a stick, compute the numeric values of both sides of the equation and verify they are equal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after proposing a stick move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘XV = XV + XV’ to ‘XV = XV = XV’ without confirming that the new equation is numerically true.

matchstick.title: Preserve valid numeral shapes
matchstick.principle: When a stick is removed from or added to a Roman numeral, the resulting shape must correspond to a valid Roman numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Any time a stick is moved to or from a numeral character.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from ‘X’ leaving a single diagonal line, which is not a valid Roman numeral.

matchstick.title: Operator stick composition
matchstick.principle: Know the exact sticks that make up each allowed operator: '+' = one vertical + one horizontal; '-' = one horizontal; '=' = two horizontals.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When converting one operator to another or when adding/removing sticks from an operator.
matchstick.example: Turning ‘+’ into ‘=’ by adding a vertical stick, resulting in an invalid operator composition.

matchstick.title: Allowed operators only
matchstick.principle: The only operators permitted are '+', '-', and '=', and the equality sign may not be turned into a disallowed symbol such as '≠'.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever an operator is altered, ensure the resulting symbol is one of the allowed operators.
matchstick.example: Replacing ‘=’ with ‘≠’ by adding a diagonal slash, using a disallowed operator.

matchstick.title: Match‑stick orientation matters
matchstick.principle: When converting one operator to another, the stick you move must have the correct orientation (vertical vs. horizontal) for the target shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any operator transformation, check the orientation of the stick being moved.
matchstick.example: Using a diagonal stick to replace a horizontal stick in the ‘=’ sign, violating orientation constraints.

matchstick.title: Do not break X or V
matchstick.principle: X and V consist of two diagonal sticks; removing one leaves an invalid shape. Never use a diagonal from X or V as the source stick.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When selecting a source stick, exclude any diagonal belonging to an X or V.
matchstick.example: Taking a diagonal stick from ‘V’ to use elsewhere, leaving an invalid ‘V’ shape.

matchstick.title: Operator‑to‑operator moves
matchstick.principle: A useful strategy is to relocate a stick from one operator to another (e.g., from ‘=’ to ‘+’) to create a new operator while keeping both operators valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When adjusting only operators does not yield a correct equality, try moving a stick between operators.
matchstick.example: Moving a horizontal stick from ‘=’ to ‘+’ without adjusting the source operator, leaving it as a single ‘-’.

matchstick.title: Limit changes to two characters
matchstick.principle: Moving a single stick can only affect the source character (which loses a stick) and the destination character (which gains a stick). No other characters may change.
matchstick.when_to_apply: During any stick move, verify that only two characters are altered.
matchstick.example: Altering three characters in one move, such as changing both a numeral and two operators simultaneously.

matchstick.title: Maintain a valid equality
matchstick.principle: The final equation must contain exactly one equality sign (or a chain of equalities) and only allowed operators.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After performing a stick move, confirm that an equality sign is still present and correctly formed.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘=’ to ‘-’ and ending up with no equality sign in the equation.

matchstick.title: Operator‑numeral stick transfers
matchstick.principle: When moving a single stick, consider transferring it between an operator and a numeral (or between two numerals) to adjust values, ensuring both source and destination remain valid characters.
matchstick.when_to_apply: If fixing the equation by only moving sticks between operators fails, explore moving a stick from an operator to a numeral or from one numeral to another.
matchstick.example: Changing ‘X = XI + I’ to ‘X = XI - I’ by removing the vertical stick from ‘+’ but not adding it to any numeral, leaving the stick unplaced.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on the visual transformation and forgets to perform the arithmetic check.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: After proposing a stick move, compute the numeric values of both sides and confirm equality before finalizing.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model removes or adds sticks without considering the set of valid numeral constructions.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Reference a list of valid Roman numeral shapes and ensure any modification yields a valid numeral.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model misremembers the exact stick composition of the allowed operators.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Recall the precise stick makeup for '+', '-', and '=' and verify the operator after any change.

matchstick.description: Moving sticks from X or V
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model tries to use any stick as a source without recognizing that X and V cannot be broken.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Never select a diagonal stick from X or V as the source for a move.

matchstick.description: Missing destination for moved stick (effectively removing a stick)
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model focuses on altering the source character but forgets that the stick must be placed onto another character.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Ensure that every moved stick is added to a valid destination character, preserving the total stick count.
